title: Abstract class vs interface
points: Abstract class: related subclasses with a clear is-a relationship that share state (fields) or code. Single inheritance only.
Interface: a contract unrelated classes can implement (can-do capability). A class can implement many.
Rule of thumb: shared state or code plus is-a means abstract class. Only a contract or multiple capabilities means interface. Default to interface.
trade: Since Java 8 interfaces can have default methods, but still no instance state. Interfaces can't have constructors; abstract classes can.
test: You have Car, Boat (share fuel logic) and Drone, Bird (both fly). Which uses an abstract class and which an interface?
answer: Car and Boat: an abstract class (Vehicle) holding shared fuel state and code. Drone and Bird: an interface (Flyable), since they are unrelated and only share a capability.

questions.question: Car and Boat share fuel-level state and a refuel() method. Drone and Bird are unrelated but both fly. What fits?
options: Interface for Car/Boat, abstract class for Drone/Bird
Abstract class for Car/Boat, interface for Drone/Bird
questions.explanation: Shared state and code with an is-a relationship means an abstract class. A shared capability across unrelated types means an interface.
